problem: The sentence 'If N is 1 000 000, one update needs 1 000 000 forward and backward passes' counts passes per sample. In vectorized deep learning frameworks one full-batch update is one large forward/backward pass over all samples or several chunked passes, not necessarily N separate passes.
fix: Reword to 'one update costs as much as 1 000 000 single-sample forward/backward passes; in a vectorized implementation it is one large pass over the whole dataset or several chunked passes.'

problem: The algorithm uses a fixed mini-batch size m and divides by m, but Q1 says an epoch has ⌈N/m⌉ updates, which implies a final incomplete mini-batch when N is not divisible by m. Dividing by m for a smaller final batch would not compute the proper average gradient.
fix: Clarify: either drop the incomplete final batch or use the actual batch size |B| in the average; change the update to θ ← θ − η (1/|B|)∑_{i∈B} ∇Li(θ).
